summary: Overall quality is strong: the notebook runs cleanly end-to-end, uses a proper train/test split and a Pipeline so preprocessing is learned only from training data, and reports a suitable metric (ROC AUC) for an imbalanced churn problem. The most important finding is that the reported performance (AUC 0.714) is internally consistent and the feature-importance narrative matches the model outputs, suggesting the results are trustworthy rather than “hand-waved.” In the interview, verify they can explain why ROC AUC was chosen, how the Pipeline/ColumnTransformer prevents data leakage, and what they would do next to make the model operational (threshold selection, calibration, and validating on a time-based split). Role requirements were not provided, so fit-to-role cannot be assessed from this review.

justifications.C1: They split into train/test before fitting any preprocessing or model (cell 7), and the preprocessing is inside a Pipeline/ColumnTransformer so scaling/OHE are learned only from training data; they also use an appropriate ranking metric (ROC AUC) for an imbalanced churn rate (~15.7%, cell 5) and explicitly handle messy decimals/categories (cell 3).
justifications.C2: The notebook executes end-to-end with no exceptions and produces stable results due to fixed random_state in the split and model (cell 7); outputs are coherent and there is no cell-order dependence evident.
justifications.C3: The conclusion’s stated AUC (0.714) matches the executed metric output exactly (cell 8 and conclusion in cell 10), and the narrative about key drivers aligns with the printed largest-magnitude coefficients (cell 9).
justifications.C4: Conclusions are directly supported by the reported AUC and coefficient inspection (cells 8–10), include a concrete business action (target monthly-contract customers with complaints) and acknowledge a key limitation with a sensible next step (threshold calibration and temporal validation, cell 10).
